test: Compute markdown dollars by year (order lines, unit_price*md/(1-md) and list-based), then break the 2022->2025 rise down by category, branch, customer, inside rep (taken_by), outside rep (account rep), and channel. Check whether net unit_price per SKU fell or held (policy change vs giveaway). Compare customers/branches/reps whose markdown rate rose most vs least (2022 vs 2024/2025) on change in order count, revenue and quote win rate. Check quote lines markdown vs won/lost outcome.
support: Markdown rise is broad (many customers/SKUs) or concentrated in some reps/branches, net price per SKU fell, and high-increase groups show no better growth in orders, revenue or win rate than flat groups.
weaken: Net price per SKU stable (markdowns offset list increases: but list is single-valued so would show as stable unit_price), or markdown targeted at quotes/segments that grew win rate or volume enough to cover the margin given up; or the markdown increase is a recording artefact (e.g. one channel or a field starting to be populated).
expect: Moderately confident (~60%) that markdowns rose broadly with no matching volume gain; some chance (~30%) the pattern is a system/recording artefact (e.g. a sudden step change in one year or channel consistent with a generator), which would make the 'giveaway' framing an interpretation rather than proven. Dollar size likely several $M/yr at standard-cost terms but the 'unbought volume' share is hard to identify causally.
